sentences.en: There was a land of cavaliers and cotton fields called the Old South.
sentences.zh: 曾经有一片土地，这里有骑士和棉田，被称为老南方。

sentences.en: Here in this pretty world, gallantry took its last bow.
sentences.zh: 在这个美丽的世界里，骑士精神迎来了它的最后一次鞠躬。

sentences.en: Here was the last ever to be seen of knights and their ladies' fair, of master and of slave.
sentences.zh: 这里最后一次见证了骑士与他们的淑女、主人与奴隶。

sentences.en: Look for it only in books, for it is no more than a dream remembered, a civilisation gone with the wind.
sentences.zh: 只能在书本中去寻找它了，因为它不过是一个被记住的梦，一个随风而逝的文明。

sentences.en: So that, Tom Holland, is the opening text of the single most successful motion picture ever made.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，这就是史上最成功的电影的开场白。

sentences.en: Gone with the Wind, released in December 1939, premiered in Atlanta, Georgia,
sentences.zh: 《乱世佳人》于1939年12月发行，在佐治亚州亚特兰大首映，

sentences.en: and went on to sell so many admissions tickets that I think one in every two people in the United States and Canada saw it,
sentences.zh: 它卖出了如此多的电影票，我想美国和加拿大的每两个人里就有一个看过，

sentences.en: and pretty much one in every two people in Britain when it ran during the Blitz a year later.
sentences.zh: 而在一年后大轰炸期间上映时，英国差不多也是每两个人里就有一个看过。

sentences.en: So are you a big Gone with the Wind fan, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你是《乱世佳人》的超级粉丝吗？

sentences.en: I've only seen it once.
sentences.zh: 我只看过一次。

sentences.en: I'm going to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: And that was a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: And all I really remember is Scarlett O'Hara going, fiddle-dee-dee.
sentences.zh: 我真正记得的只有斯嘉丽·奥哈拉在那儿说：哼，随你的便。

sentences.en: That's pretty much the limit.
sentences.zh: 差不多也就到此为止了。

sentences.en: You didn't model yourself on Rhett Butler?
sentences.zh: 你没有以瑞特·巴特勒为榜样吗？

sentences.en: I see you as a very Rhett Butler fan.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你很像瑞特·巴特勒的粉丝。

sentences.en: No, I was kind of much more an Ashley, kind of faintly wet, but sinister.
sentences.zh: 不，我其实更偏向阿希尔，有点软弱，但又透着阴险。

sentences.en: Foppish.
sentences.zh: 矫揉造作。

sentences.en: Foppish but sinister.
sentences.zh: 矫揉造作却又阴险。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But I mean, I think it's, Gone with the Wind is obviously, I suppose, with Uncle Tom's Cabin.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我觉得《乱世佳人》显然，我想，和《汤姆叔叔的小屋》一样。

sentences.en: They're kind of two great literary bookends that surround the history of the Civil War in America and its aftermath.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是两部伟大的文学基石，环绕着美国内战及其余波的历史。

sentences.en: And we've done four episodes so far on the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 我们到目前为止已经做了四集关于内战的节目。

sentences.en: And in the last episode, we looked at how it's seen today.
sentences.zh: 在上一集中，我们探讨了人们今天是怎样看待它的。

sentences.en: So all the kind of enormous contemporary resonances and ramifications that it has.
sentences.zh: 也就是它所具有的各种巨大的当代共鸣和延伸影响。

sentences.en: But essentially, we left a big gap.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，我们留下了一个巨大的空白。

sentences.en: So what happened, basically, from when the Civil War ended up to the present day?
sentences.zh: 那么，从内战结束到今天，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And in a way, Gone with the Wind is kind of the perfect way into looking at that question, I think.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，《乱世佳人》可以说是探讨这个问题的绝佳切入点，我认为。

sentences.en: And Dominic, do you know, I'm not the only person who thinks that?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你知道吗，不仅仅只有我一个人这么想？

sentences.en: No, you're not.
sentences.zh: 不，不止你一个。

sentences.en: There's someone else who thinks that.
sentences.zh: 还有别人也这么想。

sentences.en: There was a suspended book, which has just come out, I think, by the time this is released.
sentences.zh: 有一本悬念重重的书，我想在节目播出时刚出版。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: That is right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when we put, so when we advertised on Twitter asking for questions, we got a reply from Count Gabriel Thursday.
sentences.zh: 当我们发布时，我们在推特上征集问题，收到了加布里埃尔·瑟斯顿伯爵的回复。

sentences.en: Is this related to Sarah Churchill's new book?
sentences.zh: 这和萨拉·丘吉尔的新书有关吗？

sentences.en: Actually, he said Sarah Churchill's new book, but Sarah Churchill's new book, The Wrath to Come.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他说的是萨拉·丘吉尔的新书，但萨拉·丘吉尔的新书是《将临之怒》。

sentences.en: And do you know, Dominic, it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克，确实有关。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实有关。

sentences.en: Because we've got Sarah with us.
sentences.zh: 因为萨拉和我们在一起。

sentences.en: Hello, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 你好，萨拉。

sentences.en: Sarah, welcome to the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 萨拉，欢迎来到“历史的余烬”。

sentences.en: So your new book, The Wrath to Come, Gone with the Wind and the Lies America Tells.
sentences.zh: 你的新书《将临之怒：《乱世佳人》与美国所说谎言》。

sentences.en: I mean, the subtitle is giving a few clues as to your perspective on this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，副标题已经透露了你对这事的某些看法。

sentences.en: I decided not to pull any punches.
sentences.zh: 我决定不再手下留情。

sentences.en: So before we get into the lies that America tells, could we just talk about Gone with the Wind itself?
sentences.zh: 所以在我们深入探讨美国所说的谎言之前，我们能先聊聊《乱世佳人》本身吗？

sentences.en: Because I mentioned to Katie, my daughter, who will actually be coming on our next episode to talk about Love Island, which is a very, very different field of study.
sentences.zh: 因为我跟我的女儿凯蒂提过这事，她实际上会来我们下一期节目聊聊《爱情岛》，那是一个非常非常不同的研究领域。

sentences.en: And I asked her, had she heard Gone with the Wind?
sentences.zh: 我问她，听说过《乱世佳人》吗？

sentences.en: And she hadn't really.
sentences.zh: 她其实没听说过。

sentences.en: Very, very, it meant very, very little to her.
sentences.zh: 这部作品对她来说意味着非常非常少的东西。

sentences.en: She'd never seen the film, certainly never read the book.
sentences.zh: 她从未看过这部电影，当然也从未读过这本书。

sentences.en: So for people who may not be familiar with it, could you just give us a sense of how colossal a publishing and then a cinematic phenomenon it was, is?
sentences.zh: 所以对于可能不熟悉它的人，你能跟我们讲讲它曾经以及现在是一部多么庞大的出版和电影现象吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: And I'll say that size of its impact is, in a sense, still registered by the fact that even though your daughter has never seen it or read it, she still has faintly heard of it.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，它的影响力之大，从某种意义上仍然体现在：尽管你的女儿从未看过或读过它，她依然隐约听说过它。

sentences.en: So we can flip it on its head and say it's still out there.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以反过来想，它依然存在。

sentences.en: People are aware of it, even if only, you know, indirectly and ambiently.
sentences.zh: 人们都知道它，哪怕只是（你知道的）间接和潜移默化地知道。

sentences.en: And that is still the outward reverberations of a century of, as you say, colossal impact.
sentences.zh: 这依然是一个世纪以来（正如你所说）巨大影响力的向外回响。

sentences.en: So when the novel was published in 1936 and it became an instant word of mouth phenomenon, it didn't have a massive publicity campaign behind it in some of the ways that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以当这部小说在1936年出版时，它立刻成为了口碑相传的现象级作品，它背后并没有那种我们现在习惯了的大规模宣传造势活动，

sentences.en: we're now accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: It was a genuine popular hit and it instantly became the book that everybody was reading and everybody was talking about in the United States.
sentences.zh: 它是一部真正的畅销热门作品，在美国瞬间成为了所有人都在阅读、所有人都在讨论的书。

sentences.en: So it was written by a woman called Margaret Mitchell.
sentences.zh: 这本书的作者是一位名叫玛格丽特·米ッチェルの女性。（注：Mitchell）

sentences.en: And you said Gone with the Wind is a good way into the bridging the gap.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说《乱世佳人》是弥合鸿沟的一个好切入点。

sentences.en: But so is Margaret Mitchell, because Margaret Mitchell was born in 1900 and she died in 1949.
sentences.zh: 但玛格丽特·米切尔也是，因为她生于1900年，卒于1949年。

sentences.en: So her life, you know, perfectly spans the first half of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以她的生平（你知道的）完美地跨越了20世纪的上半叶。

sentences.en: And she helps us also cover some of these key milestones in American history that bridge the Civil War until now.
sentences.zh: 她也帮助我们涵盖了美国历史上连接内战与现在的那些关键里程碑。

sentences.en: She was born in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 她出生于亚特兰大。

sentences.en: And the famous character of Scarlett O'Hara, if anybody has heard of Gone with the Wind, they've probably heard of Scarlett O'Hara, the novel's heroine.
sentences.zh: 而著名的角色斯嘉丽·奥哈拉——如果有人听说过《乱世佳人》，他们大概就听说过小说中的女主角斯嘉丽·奥哈拉。

sentences.en: And Margaret Mitchell based Scarlett O'Hara on her own grandmother, who was born into a slaveholding plantation just outside of Atlanta and bitterly resented the loss of her power,
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·米切尔是以她自己的祖母为原型塑造斯嘉丽·奥哈拉的，她的祖母出生于亚特兰大郊外的一个蓄奴种植园，终生都对失去权力、

sentences.en: her property, including her human property for the rest of her life.
sentences.zh: 财产——包括她的“人类财产”——感到无比怨恨。

sentences.en: And raised her granddaughter with the stories of the grandeur of the Old South of life before the Yankees came and ruined everything for the white slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 她用老南方奢华生活的故事抚育孙女，讲述北方佬到来并毁掉白人奴隶主一切之前的生活。

sentences.en: And Margaret Mitchell grew up on these legends and Gone with the Wind is, in one sense, a kind of compendium of these legends.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·米切尔伴随着这些传奇故事长大，从某种意义上说，《乱世佳人》就是这些传奇故事的大合集。

sentences.en: But it's also important to say that from Margaret Mitchell's point of view, she thought she was doing something more realistic.
sentences.zh: 但同样重要的是，从玛格丽特·米切尔的角度来看，她认为自己在做一件更现实的事情。

sentences.en: And I'm sure we'll get into that at various points.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们会在不同阶段深入探讨这一点。

sentences.en: So in her mind, she was telling more realistic account of the Civil War years in a popular novel.
sentences.zh: 所以在她看来，她是在一部通俗小说中对内战岁月做出更现实的叙述。

sentences.en: The novel became a massive bestseller in the United States, and then it exported very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 这部小说在美国成为了超级畅销书，然后非常非常快地向海外输出。

sentences.en: And it went across Europe as fascism was on the rise.
sentences.zh: 它随着法西斯的崛起而传遍了整个欧洲。

sentences.en: And in fact, not only was it loved by people who were starting to see incursions by, you know, Hitler and Mussolini, but it was also loved reportedly by, and indeed, documentedly,
sentences.zh: 事实上，不仅那些开始看到希特勒和墨索里尼（你知道的）侵略行径的人喜爱它，据报道，甚至有据可查的是，

sentences.en: by many Nazis as well.
sentences.zh: 许多纳粹分子也同样喜爱它。

sentences.en: Eventually, the Nazis banned it.
sentences.zh: 最终，纳粹禁了它。

sentences.en: But so, I mean, it was popular everywhere, is my point, as it started to spread.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，随着它开始传播，它到处都很受欢迎，这就是我的观点。

sentences.en: And then the rights to the novel were instantly acquired by the legendary producer David Selznick, who understood publicity very, very well.
sentences.zh: 随后，小说的版权立刻被传奇制片人大卫·塞尔兹尼克买下，他非常非常懂宣传。

sentences.en: And he began a campaign to find the perfect Scarlett O'Hara.
sentences.zh: 他发起了一场寻找完美斯嘉丽·奥哈拉的活动。

sentences.en: It was called The Search for Scarlett.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“寻找斯嘉丽”。

sentences.en: This became a massive publicity campaign that filled papers and film magazines and the equivalent of social media at the time.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一场大规模的宣传活动，占据了报纸、电影杂志以及当时相当于社交媒体的版面。

sentences.en: And everybody wanted to be Scarlett.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想成为斯嘉丽。

sentences.en: And so the idea was, you know, that millions could try out across the country, and maybe he would find an unknown.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的构想是（你知道的），全国各地的千百万人都可以试镜，也许他能找到一个新人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you could be an amateur actress and still try to be Scarlett O'Hara.
sentences.zh: 因此（你知道的）你哪怕是个业余女演员，也可以去尝试扮演斯嘉丽·奥哈拉。

sentences.en: And he told all of these publicity stories about how he was going to cast the story and who would be the perfect stars of this, you know, incredibly popular novel.
sentences.zh: 他散布了所有这些宣传故事，讲述他将如何为这个故事选角，谁会成为这部（你知道的）极其受欢迎的小说的完美明星。

sentences.en: So that by the time the film was released at the end of 1939, it was backed by this three-year relentless publicity campaign.
sentences.zh: 因此，当这部电影在1939年底上映时，它背后有这场历时三年的不间断宣传活动作支撑。

sentences.en: And it became an absolutely smash hit phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 它成为了一个绝对轰动的现象级大热门。

sentences.en: They said it was the greatest motion picture ever made, the greatest Hollywood movie.
sentences.zh: 人们说这是有史以来最伟大的电影，最伟大的好莱坞电影。

sentences.en: And it should be said, 1939 remains the classic year of Hollywood cinema, a year of greats like The Wizard of Oz and many other classic movies.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，1939年依然是好莱坞电影的经典年份，这一年诞生了《绿野仙踪》以及许多其他经典电影等巨作。

sentences.en: But Gone with the Wind beat them all.
sentences.zh: 但《乱世佳人》打败了它们所有人。

sentences.en: And it was the movie that everybody wanted to see.
sentences.zh: 它是人人都想看的电影。

sentences.en: And again, it exported very quickly through Europe, through war-torn Europe.
sentences.zh: 同样，它通过欧洲、通过饱受战争蹂躏的欧洲非常迅速地输出了出去。

sentences.en: And as Dominic mentioned, at the top was incredibly popular during the Blitz, for example.
sentences.zh: 正如多米尼克在开头提到的，例如在大轰炸期间，它极其受欢迎。

sentences.en: People were queuing up in Leicester Square as bombs burned, you know, from the overnight bombings, or fires burned, I mean.
sentences.zh: 当炸弹（你知道的）在夜间轰炸中燃烧，或者说火焰燃烧时，人们在莱斯特广场排着长队。

sentences.en: So, Sarah, one of the iconic scenes in the film is when Atlanta gets burnt by General Sherman.
sentences.zh: 所以，萨拉，电影中标志性的场景之一就是亚特兰大被谢尔曼将军烧毁。

sentences.en: Yeah, we talked about that in the Civil War narrative, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 对，我们在内战叙事中聊过这个，对吧？

sentences.en: Sherman's marched to the sea in the scorched earth policy.
sentences.zh: 谢尔曼的进军大海与焦土政策。

sentences.en: And I learned from your book that Margaret Mitchell's grandmother had lived through the burning of Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 我从你的书里得知，玛格丽特·米切尔的祖母曾亲历亚特兰大的大火。

sentences.en: So, presumably, that is something that is on the minds of people in the Blitz.
sentences.zh: 所以，可以想象，这也是经历大轰炸的人们脑海中所想的事情。

sentences.en: They're kind of, they're going in and they're seeing Atlanta burn, and then they're coming out and they're seeing the London skyline lit up with fire.
sentences.zh: 他们一边（你知道的）走进去看亚特兰大燃烧，一边走出来看到伦敦的天际线被火焰照亮。

sentences.en: And one of the kind of the great theme in Gone with the Wind is, I mean, Scarlett O'Hara is a, I mean, she's a piece of work in a way, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 《乱世佳人》的核心主题之一——我的意思是，斯嘉丽·奥哈拉这个人（你知道的）某种程度上真是个奇葩，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, she's not a conventional heroine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她可不是传统意义上的女主角。

sentences.en: She's what you would call a baggage.
sentences.zh: 她就是你所谓的“无赖荡妇”。

sentences.en: She is indeed a baggage.
sentences.zh: 她确实是个“无赖荡妇”。

sentences.en: She's very 18th century baggage.
sentences.zh: 非常有18世纪风格的“无赖荡妇”。

sentences.en: But her kind of great life's mission is to get back her family plantation, which is called Tara, which was this kind of,
sentences.zh: 但她伟大的人生使命是夺回她的家族种植园，那个地方叫塔拉，曾经是那种——

sentences.en: it's where the land of cavaliers and cotton fields and all that kind of stuff with which it opens.
sentences.zh: 这就是片头出现的骑士与棉田的土地以及所有那些乱七八糟的东西。

sentences.en: And then it gets destroyed in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 然后它在内战中被摧毁了。

sentences.en: And her life's mission is to get it back and get her life back on an even keel.
sentences.zh: 她的人生使命就是把它夺回来，让生活重回正轨。

sentences.en: So presumably this is the message that people during war-torn Europe are picking up on.
sentences.zh: 所以可以想象，这就是饱受战争蹂躏的欧洲人所领会到的信息。

sentences.en: It's this idea that things will get back to normal.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种一切都会恢复正常的想法。

sentences.en: I just have to dig deep and I will be able to get it back.
sentences.zh: 我只要咬紧牙关，就能把它夺回来。

sentences.en: It's a story about resilience and it's a story about survivalism, fundamentally on its most emotional level.
sentences.zh: 从最感性的层面上讲，这基本上是一个关于韧性的故事，一个关于生存主义的故事。

sentences.en: And that's what people respond to.
sentences.zh: 这也是人们所产生共鸣的地方。

sentences.en: And it's worth, before we skip to war-torn Europe, remembering that it hits America in the middle of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 在我们跳到饱受战争蹂躏的欧洲之前，值得记住的是，它在美国大萧条中期上映。

sentences.en: So Americans who are struggling, you know, people on drought-stricken farms who are struggling themselves with famine, Scarlet has to overcome hunger.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些挣扎求生的美国人（你知道的），那些在干旱农场上面临饥荒挣扎的农夫，斯嘉丽必须战胜饥饿。

sentences.en: She has to, yeah, and she overcomes the blight of her farm.
sentences.zh: 她必须——是的，她战胜了她农场的荒芜。

sentences.en: And so first you have the blight of the Great Depression and then you have the blight of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以你首先面对的是大萧条的荒芜，然后是第二次世界大战的荒芜。

sentences.en: And in both of these two historical cataclysms, this story about human endurance and survival and sheer defiance, determination.
sentences.zh: 在这两场历史大灾难中，这个关于人类坚韧、生存以及纯粹反抗、决心的故事，

sentences.en: Scarlet is determined no matter what.
sentences.zh: 斯嘉丽无论如何都无比坚定。

sentences.en: And as you said, what makes her a baggage is that she's totally unscrupulous.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，让她成为一个“无赖荡妇”的原因在于她完全毫无道德底线。

sentences.en: And she will literally do anything.
sentences.zh: 她字面意义上什么都干得出来。

sentences.en: So, you know, at one point she considers becoming Rhett Butler's mistress.
sentences.zh: 所以，（你知道的）在某个时刻，她考虑成为瑞特·巴特勒的情妇。

sentences.en: If that's what it's going to take, that's what she'll do.
sentences.zh: 如果非得如此才能达到目的，她就会这么做。

sentences.en: She will sell herself in marriage.
sentences.zh: 她会通过结婚来把自己卖掉。

sentences.en: She does sell herself in marriage.
sentences.zh: 她确实通过结婚把自己卖了。

sentences.en: She's perfectly happy, not happy, but she's prepared to do whatever it takes.
sentences.zh: 她非常乐意——虽说不上高兴，但她做好了付出任何代价的准备。

sentences.en: And that's what people have always responded to with Scarlet O'Hara.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们对斯嘉丽·奥哈拉一直以来的共鸣所在。

sentences.en: And the other thing I think that's important to say at the top in terms of its popularity, Scarlet O'Hara, and I talk about this at some length in the book,
sentences.zh: 我认为在开头关于其受欢迎程度方面同样重要的另一件事是，斯嘉丽·奥哈拉——我在书中对此进行了相当篇幅的讨论——

sentences.en: is really the first American every woman.
sentences.zh: 真的是第一位美国“每个女性”。

sentences.en: The first popular character who everybody identifies with but who's female.
sentences.zh: 第一个人人都产生共鸣、但性别是女性的流行角色。

sentences.en: And that's for women, that's incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 这对于女性来说，具有极其重大的意义。

sentences.en: And so for a lot of women, she became this very interesting feminist figure because she's powerful.
sentences.zh: 因此对许多女性而言，她成了一个非常有趣的女性主义人物，因为她很强大。

sentences.en: And as we said, she's defiant, but she's also deeply problematic.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，她桀骜不驯，但她也存在着深深的争议。

sentences.en: And, you know, and she's a horrible person in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 而且（你知道的）在很多方面她都是个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: But that makes her human.
sentences.zh: 但这让她显得有血有肉。

sentences.en: And that, again, makes her relatable.
sentences.zh: 这也再次让她显得真实可感。

sentences.en: And so she's an important landmark in popular culture for women as well.
sentences.zh: 所以她对女性大众文化而言也是一个重要的里程碑。

sentences.en: So we had a comment from Sarah Jones who says, I think it's an important film because it's a rare film from the female gaze.
sentences.zh: 萨拉·琼斯曾评论说，我认为这是一部重要的电影，因为这是一部罕见的从女性凝视出发的电影。

sentences.en: It's a war film with not a single battle scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一部连一个战斗场面都没有的战争片。

sentences.en: It's a woman's experience of war.
sentences.zh: 这是女性眼中的战争体验。

sentences.en: And that's actually pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 这其实相当罕见。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And, again, this was a way that, again, the story was received, first the novel and then the film, very strongly among the first readers.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也正是这个故事——先是小说，然后是电影——在第一批读者中产生强烈反响的方式。

sentences.en: Its early reception was that it was an anti-war novel.
sentences.zh: 它早期的反响是一部反战小说。

sentences.en: And that was really important in that what you see is the cost of war for civilians.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要，因为你看到的是战争对平民造成的代价。

sentences.en: It's that you don't see – it's a Civil War novel with no battles.
sentences.zh: 你看不到的是——这是一部没有战争场面的内战小说。

sentences.en: You don't see any battles.
sentences.zh: 你看不到任何战争。

sentences.en: Nobody goes to the battles.
sentences.zh: 没有人去参加战争。

sentences.en: You just see the casualties.
sentences.zh: 你看到的只是伤亡。

sentences.en: You see the casualties.
sentences.zh: 你看到的都是伤亡。

sentences.en: It's kind of famous shot, isn't it, which is actually on the cover of your book.
sentences.zh: 这是一个挺有名的镜头，对吧，实际上就在你书的封面上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Where is it – Scarlett has gone to try and get someone to help with a pregnancy, with a birth character.
sentences.zh: 那是哪里——斯嘉丽去试图找人帮忙接生，接生一个角色。

sentences.en: With a labor, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 去接生，对，没错。

sentences.en: With a labor.
sentences.zh: 去接生。

sentences.en: And the camera pulls back and you see this kind of vast field full of – Of carnage.
sentences.zh: 然后镜头拉远，你看到这种广阔的田野上满是——全都是血腥的尸体。

sentences.en: So she goes to the train depot to try to find the doctor, and the doctor is tending the war, wounded and dying.
sentences.zh: 所以她去火车站试图找医生，而医生正在照顾战争中的伤员和垂死的人。

sentences.en: And Scarlett is being very selfish and saying that she has to help her friend, Melanie, her sister-in-law, give birth.
sentences.zh: 而斯嘉丽却非常自私地说，她必须帮她的朋友梅兰妮，也就是她的嫂子生孩子。

sentences.en: And the doctor is like, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 结果医生说，你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: I've got thousands of dying soldiers.
sentences.zh: 我有成千上万快要死去的士兵。

sentences.en: You're going to have to handle the pregnancy on your own.
sentences.zh: 你得自己去搞定分娩了。

sentences.en: And then, as you say, the camera pans back to these scores and scores and scores of wounded and dying soldiers to give a sense of the scale of the carnage.
sentences.zh: 然后，正如你所说，镜头平移回到这些成群结队、数不胜数的受伤和垂死的士兵身上，来展现血腥场面的规模感。

sentences.en: And, Sarah, just one last thing.
sentences.zh: 萨拉，还有最后一件事。

sentences.en: You mentioned Rhett Butler, played by Clark Gable in the film.
sentences.zh: 你提到了瑞特·巴特勒，在电影中由克拉克·盖博饰演。

sentences.en: Probably the most famous line, maybe in the whole of Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最著名的一句台词，也许是整个好莱坞历史上最著名的。

sentences.en: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn with which it ends.
sentences.zh: “坦白说，亲爱的，我不在乎，”电影就是这样结束的。

sentences.en: It's still the most – it's still on, you know, things like the American Film Institute's list of most famous movie quotes.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是——它仍然在诸如美国电影学会的最著名电影台词榜单上。

sentences.en: That is still the most famous movie quote to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，那仍然是最著名的电影台词。

sentences.en: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，亲爱的，我不在乎。

sentences.en: So just before we move on from Gone with the Wind and the plot and everything, could you just tell us briefly about Scarlett O'Hara and men and what her – because that's also,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们继续探讨《乱世佳人》的剧情和一切之前，你能简要给我们讲讲斯嘉丽·欧哈拉和男人们，以及她——因为这也是，

sentences.en: I mean, the key part of the plot, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，剧情的关键部分，对吧？

sentences.en: And there are two in particular.
sentences.zh: 这里特别有两个男人。

sentences.en: There's the guy who she thinks she's in love with and then there's the guy who she discovers actually all along she was in love with.
sentences.zh: 一个是她以为自己爱的人，另一个是她发现其实自己一直都爱的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Scarlett is a kind of heroine chasing the wrong hero for most of the story.
sentences.zh: 所以斯嘉丽在故事的大部分时间里是一个追逐错误英雄的女主角。

sentences.en: So she thinks that she loves Ashley.
sentences.zh: 所以她以为自己爱的是阿什利。

sentences.en: Every reader of the novel and, you know, the audience of the film can see instantly that Ashley is not the right man for her.
sentences.zh: 小说的每一位读者，还有，你知道的，电影的观众都能一眼看出阿什利并不是适合她的男人。

sentences.en: And that Rhett Butler, who is her twin in kind of every way, they're complete kindred spirits.
sentences.zh: 而瑞特·巴特勒，在某种程度上可以说是她的另一个自己，他们完全是志同道合的灵魂。

sentences.en: They're both rogues and renegades and they're scoundrels, but they're sort of lovable rogues and they're made for each other.
sentences.zh: 他们都是无赖、叛逆者和恶棍，但他们是那种讨人喜欢的无赖，他们天生是一对。

sentences.en: And Rhett knows that.
sentences.zh: 而瑞特知道这一点。

sentences.en: He's older and wiser and very sexy.
sentences.zh: 他年长、成熟且非常性感。

sentences.en: And so he's the kind of masterful man.
sentences.zh: 所以他是那种很有掌控力的男人。

sentences.en: And Scarlett is beautiful, but she doesn't have any emotional self-knowledge, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 而斯嘉丽虽然漂亮，但说实话，她对自己的情感一无所知。

sentences.en: And so the story is, you know, it spans, I think I should know this, but it spans 13 years.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事，你知道的，跨越了——我想我应该知道，但它跨越了13年。

sentences.en: And she and as I say, at one point in my book, you know, she literally learns nothing except that she loved the wrong man.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，在我的书中的某处，你知道的，她实际上什么也没学会，除了她爱错了人。

sentences.en: And it takes her over a decade to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 她花了十多年的时间才弄明白这一点。

sentences.en: So Ashley, as you said at the beginning, Tom is this kind of he's he's you called him wet.
sentences.zh: 所以阿什利，正如你一开始所说的，汤姆，这家伙——你称他为软弱。

sentences.en: But he is he's nostalgic.
sentences.zh: 但他——他很怀旧。

sentences.en: He represents the old South and he represents this old way of life.
sentences.zh: 他代表了旧南方，代表了这种旧的生活方式。

sentences.en: And he's idealistic and and a bit naive.
sentences.zh: 而且他很理想主义，还有点天真。

sentences.en: And and he reads books and he's ineffective.
sentences.zh: 他饱读诗书却没什么实际能力。

sentences.en: And and but he's handsome.
sentences.zh: 但他长得很帅。

sentences.en: And so Scarlett kind of falls for him as a young girl and then never changes her mind until the very end.
sentences.zh: 所以斯嘉丽在年轻时就迷上了他，然后直到最后也从未改变心意。

sentences.en: Rhett is this dashing, as I say, he's this rogue who comes in and he's he's the black sheep of his of his old aristocratic family.
sentences.zh: 而瑞特就像我说的，是个潇洒的浪子，他出场了，他是他那个古老贵族家庭里的异类。

sentences.en: And he recognizes that Scarlett is a kindred spirit, but she's too pigheaded.
sentences.zh: 他认出斯嘉丽是个同道中人，但她太顽固了。

sentences.en: And so he spends most of the story trying to convince her that, you know, that he's right for her.
sentences.zh: 所以他大半个故事都在试图说服她，你知道的，他是最适合她的人。

sentences.en: But he won't.
sentences.zh: 但他不会这么做。

sentences.en: He's too proud, of course, to let his real feelings show.
sentences.zh: 当然，他太骄傲了，不肯表露真实的感情。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's so famous about Gone with the Wind as a story is that as a romance, it's a very rare thing in that it's not star crossed.
sentences.zh: 《乱世佳人》作为一部小说之所以如此著名，原因之一在于作为一部爱情故事，它非常罕见，因为他们并不是苦命鸳鸯。

sentences.en: They don't die, but they don't reconcile either.
sentences.zh: 他们没有死，但也没有重归于好。

sentences.en: Rhett walks out on her.
sentences.zh: 瑞特抛弃了她一走了之。

sentences.en: And that's when he says, frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时他说出了：“坦白说，亲爱的，我不在乎。”

sentences.en: It's the answer to her question.
sentences.zh: 这是对她问题的回答。

sentences.en: If you leave me, where shall I go?
sentences.zh: 如果你离开我，我该去哪里？

sentences.en: Oh, what shall I do?
sentences.zh: 哦，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: And he says, I don't care, walks out the door.
sentences.zh: 而他说，我不在乎，然后走出了大门。

sentences.en: And that's the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 故事就这样结束了。

sentences.en: And so it's a very famous ending for romance.
sentences.zh: 所以对于爱情故事来说，这是一个非常著名的结局。

sentences.en: The hero walks out, is up yours.
sentences.zh: 男主角一走了之，态度极其强硬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, Sarah, the subtitle of your book is The Lies America Tells.
sentences.zh: 那么，萨拉，你这本书的副标题是《美国讲述的谎言》。

sentences.en: And one way to maybe start getting towards that part of the story is to talk about the film's premiere.
sentences.zh: 要开始切入故事的那个部分，其中一个方法就是谈谈这部电影的首映式。

sentences.en: So it premieres in Atlanta, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 它在佐治亚州亚特兰大首映。

sentences.en: There are 300,000 people, I think, on the streets for this huge procession.
sentences.zh: 我想有30万人涌上街头参加这场盛大的游行。

sentences.en: People dress up, don't they, in costume from the Civil War era.
sentences.zh: 人们都盛装打扮，穿着内战时期的服装，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a state holiday.
sentences.zh: 这是一个州立节日。

sentences.en: It's a huge moment for the city of Atlanta, which is this kind of booming New South city, for Georgia, for the old Confederacy.
sentences.zh: 对于亚特兰大这座蓬勃发展的南方新城市、对于佐治亚州、对于旧邦联来说，这是一个重大的时刻。

sentences.en: And it seems like, you could say, a lovely moment of reconciliation between North and South.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这似乎是南北双方实现和解的美好时刻。

sentences.en: But obviously, there are all kinds of shadows.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，这里面存在着各种阴暗面。

sentences.en: A great example of that is the fact that one of the stars, Hattie McDaniel, is not welcome at the premiere.
sentences.zh: 其中一个很好的例子就是，主演之一的哈蒂·麦克丹尼尔不被欢迎参加首映式。

sentences.en: None of the black cast was welcome at the premiere.
sentences.zh: 所有的黑人演员都不受欢迎参加首映式。

sentences.en: So she's playing Mammy, who is the maid at Tara.
sentences.zh: 所以她饰演的是“妈咪”（Mammy），也就是塔拉庄园的女佣。

sentences.en: So the housekeeper and Scarlet's nurse, and the most important black character in the film.
sentences.zh: 也就是管家兼斯嘉丽的奶妈，也是电影中最重要的黑人角色。

sentences.en: Hattie McDaniel would, of course, go on to become the first African-American actor to win an Academy Award for her performance in Gone with the Wind.
sentences.zh: 当然，哈蒂·麦克丹尼尔后来凭借在《乱世佳人》中的表演，成为了第一位获得奥斯卡奖的非裔美国演员。

sentences.en: And exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So people need to remember that when the movie came out, segregation was still in force in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 所以人们需要记住，当这部电影上映时，亚特兰大仍然实行种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: The black cast was not invited to the premiere.
sentences.zh: 黑人演员没有被邀请参加首映式。

sentences.en: So you have pictures of this all-white audience.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到这些全白人观众的照片。

sentences.en: And when, you know, Dominic, you say that they were dressing up in Civil War costume.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，当你说他们在穿着内战时期的服装时。

sentences.en: Well, it was cosplay, but it was cosplay as slave owners.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是角色扮演，但扮演的是奴隶主。

sentences.en: So they weren't dressing up as slaves.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不是扮成奴隶。

sentences.en: They were dressing up as slave holders.
sentences.zh: 他们扮的是奴隶主。

sentences.en: And they were, you know, white women dressing up as Southern bells in the big hoop skirts and, you know, men dressed up in, you know, 19th century clothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，白人妇女们打扮成穿着大裙撑的南方淑女，男人们穿着19世纪的服装。

sentences.en: But that was so that you could role play that the fantasy was that you still owned a plantation with hundreds of African-American slaves.
sentences.zh: 但那是为了让他们能够角色扮演，那种幻想是——你依然拥有一个拥有数百名非裔美国奴隶的种植园。

sentences.en: And so just beyond those happy photographs of white Hollywood stars and white audiences are black picket lines.
sentences.zh: 所以在白人好莱坞明星和白人观众那些快乐的照片背后，是黑人的抗议纠察线。

sentences.en: African-Americans picketing this because it was segregated, because they said this rightly, they said this is romanticizing slavery.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人对此进行抗议，因为这是种族隔离的，因为他们言之凿凿地指出，这是在美化奴隶制。

sentences.en: This is romanticizing racial violence.
sentences.zh: 这是在美化种族暴力。

sentences.en: And it is and it's glorifying what is still, you know, still exists as racial inequality and segregation at the time.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，它在美化当时依然存在的种族不平等和种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: And so what you have is a black cast who's and a white culture that's insisting and a story that says that slavery wasn't bad for America.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是，一方面是黑人群体，另一方面是白人文化在坚称——并且有一个故事在宣称，奴隶制对美国并没有坏处。

sentences.en: That's basically the insistence here is that it's all over.
sentences.zh: 这里基本上一直在强调的是，这一切都过去了。

sentences.en: It's all fine.
sentences.zh: 一切都很好。

sentences.en: We can move on and we can just tell this happy story about what slavery was like.
sentences.zh: 我们可以向前看，我们可以讲述一个关于奴隶制是什么样子的快乐故事。

sentences.en: And and so black people are literally being told that slavery inflicted no costs on American culture at the same moment that black people are being excluded from attending a film in which they feature.
sentences.zh: 因此，正当黑人被排挤在他们有份出演的电影首映礼之外时，他们却字面意义上被告知，奴隶制没有给美国文化造成任何代价。

sentences.en: And in which some, as I say, some of these actors, you know, we're going to give award winning performances.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，在这些演员中，有些人将会贡献出获奖级别的表演。

sentences.en: And when Hattie and it's important to say this wasn't just in the South.
sentences.zh: 当哈蒂——必须指出的是，这不仅仅发生在南方。

sentences.en: So when Hattie McDaniel won that award, she did so at a segregated ceremony, Oscar ceremony, from which she had originally been barred from attending that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以当哈蒂·麦克丹尼尔赢得那个奖项时，她是在一个实行种族隔离的奥斯卡颁奖典礼上领奖的，而她最初甚至被禁止出席那个典礼。

sentences.en: And David Selznick, the producer, had to pull strings to get her invited to the Coconut Grove where the ceremony was held because it was segregated, too.
sentences.zh: 制片人大卫·塞尔兹尼克不得不动用各种关系，才让她得以受邀前往举办颁奖典礼的椰林俱乐部，因为那里也实行种族隔离。

sentences.en: And that was in Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 而且那是在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: Really naive question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真的很天真的问题。

sentences.en: I thought segregation was it happened in the South.
sentences.zh: 我以为种族隔离只发生在南方。

sentences.en: No, it was across the United States.
sentences.zh: 不，它是全美范围的。

sentences.en: So it was it was known as the color bar.

sentences.en: So here's a question, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 所以有个问题，萨拉。

sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么南方白人——你不需要是个天才就能弄明白为什么南方白人喜欢《乱世佳人》。

sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 我确信我们会去剖析其中所有的深层问题。

sentences.en: The question is why people in the North, you know, we've done four episodes on the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 问题在于为什么北方的人——我们已经做了四期关于内战的节目。

sentences.en: We've talked about the massive casualty rates, the horrendous treatments of prisoners, all of these things.

sentences.zh: 这是在人们的有生记忆之内的。

sentences.en: You know, you can still be old enough to remember the Civil War in the late 1930s.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在20世纪30年代末，你可能还够老到能记得内战。

sentences.en: I think just about.

sentences.en: So why is it that people in I don't know, in Boston, in New York, in Chicago, wherever are flocking to this film in a in in apparently, you know,
sentences.zh: 那么为什么在——我不知道，在波士顿、纽约、芝加哥或其他什么地方的人们，会蜂拥去看这部电影，而且显然是以一种，

sentences.zh: 一种毫无负罪感、毫无羞耻感、毫无批判性的方式，津津有味地看着南方淑女，喜爱饰演斯嘉丽·欧哈拉的费雯·丽，喜爱克拉克·盖博？

sentences.zh: 还是我弄错了？

sentences.zh: 不，你没有弄错。

sentences.zh: 它是多么不准确，而且它有着极大的问题。

sentences.en: And the answer to that, I can I can put it very briefly as an assertion, but people may or may not believe me.
sentences.zh: 而对于这个问题的答案，我可以非常简短地做一个断言，大家或许会相信我，或许不会。

sentences.en: But part of what my book is about is making the case for what I'm now going to assert,
sentences.zh: 但我的书所要表达的部分内容，就是为我接下来要阐述的观点进行论证，

sentences.en: which is that the reason they were OK with it was because the country reunited after the Civil War around white supremacism.
sentences.zh: 也就是：他们之所以能接受这部电影，是因为这个国家在内战后是以白人至上主义为基础重新联合起来的。

sentences.en: Because the key thing here to remember is that, first of all, it's not even true that the war was fought by the North to end slavery.
sentences.zh: 因为这里需要记住的关键一点是，首先，北方为废除奴隶制而进行这场战争甚至都不是真的。

sentences.en: They didn't begin the war, as I'm sure you've covered in your in your podcast, which have not yet gone out yet, which is why I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有挑起这场战争——我确信你们已经在播客里讨论过了，虽然这期节目还没上线，所以我并不知道。

sentences.en: I will, of course, be avidly listening.
sentences.zh: 当然，我会非常热切地收听。

sentences.en: But that, you know, they didn't.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，他们确实没有。

sentences.zh: 北方参战并不是为了废除奴隶制。

sentences.zh: 它参战是为了维系联邦的统一。

sentences.en: And the fight, the conflict was over the question of slavery.
sentences.zh: 而这场斗争、这个冲突是围绕着奴隶制的问题展开的。

sentences.en: But they they didn't enter it to create abolition, to affect abolition.

sentences.en: As I say in the book, that's why they were the Union army and not the abolitionists.
sentences.zh: 正如我在书中所说，这就是为什么他们是联邦军队，而不是废奴主义者。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they the fight originally was to hold the country together.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最初的斗争是为了维系国家的统一。

sentences.en: And abolition became a necessary thing to do in order for that to happen.
sentences.zh: 而为了实现这一点，废奴成了一件不得不做的事。

sentences.en: And certainly the fight was over the the expansion of slavery and whether slavery should continue in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且这场斗争当然是关于奴隶制的扩张，以及奴隶制是否应在美国继续存在。

sentences.en: That was absolutely the core of the battle.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是这场战役的核心。

sentences.zh: 但关键在于，你可以认为奴隶制是错误的，同时却又能接受种族主义。

sentences.en: And that's the key is that you can think that black people are inherently inferior and just think that slavery is a moral abomination.
sentences.zh: 关键就在于，你可以认为黑人天生低人一等，同时又觉得奴隶制是一种道德上的令人发指的行为。

sentences.en: So you may think that black people have a right to not be enslaved, but not that they are your equal and not that they have a right to all of the same entitlement.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会认为黑人有不被奴役的权利，但并不认为他们是你的平等之人，也不认为他们有权享有与你完全相同的权利。

sentences.en: And prerogatives that you have.
sentences.zh: 以及你所拥有的特权。

sentences.en: And so over several decades between and we should give people the anchor dates again.

sentences.en: And because America is, you know, a lovely place anyway.

sentences.zh: 于是大家都聚在一起，开始相信奴隶制其实算得了什么大问题。

sentences.zh: 带着这种心态，你就可以去看《乱世佳人》并享受它了。

sentences.zh: 所以，萨拉，在你的书中，你做了一个总结：战争废除了奴隶制，但白人至上主义没有。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.

sentences.zh: 那么，《乱世佳人》为这一进程映照出了怎样的一面镜子？

sentences.zh: 接着，玛格丽特·米ッチェル（玛格丽特·米切尔）举起这面镜子这一事实意味着什么？

sentences.zh: 这将是一个简短的回答。

sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，在你的书里，你是在说，你知道的，

sentences.zh: 所以我知道，而我无法回答这个问题。

sentences.zh: 所以我的回答是，它所讲述的真实之处在于，它展现了南方白人的心态。

sentences.en: And that's what we had.

sentences.zh: 我想用来重新构建这一观点的关键在于，不断提醒我的读者：这是一场由思嘉的社会所发动的战争，目的是为了捍卫一种无法辩护的生活方式，

sentences.zh: 思嘉以及她的朋友和家人非常把自己当作受害者。

sentences.zh: 正是他们在这个整个过程中受到了迫害。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在讨论开始时说过，她想让自己的生活重回正轨。

sentences.en: That's her point of view.
sentences.zh: 那是她的观点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But my point of view is that she wants to reclaim her power.
sentences.zh: 但我的观点是，她想要夺回自己的权力。

sentences.en: She lost all of her power and she wants it back.
sentences.zh: 她失去了所有的权力，而她想要把它夺回来。

sentences.en: She wants to be rich again.
sentences.zh: 她想再次变得富有。

sentences.en: She wants to have slaves again and she can't have slaves legally.
sentences.zh: 她想再次拥有奴隶，虽然她在法律上不能拥有奴隶。

sentences.en: But what the story shows is, and I kind of give lots of examples of this, is that Scarlett's fantasies of power are never just getting her money and her house back.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事所展示的——我对此举了很多例子——是思嘉对权力的幻想从来不只是拿回她的金钱和房子。

sentences.en: They're always entangled with fantasies of having black people working the land again.
sentences.zh: 它们总是与让黑人重新在这片土地上劳动的幻想交织在一起。

sentences.en: And she says that in so many words over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 她一遍又一遍、反反复复地用最明确的语言表达了这一点。

sentences.en: She says she would never feel like a lady again until black hands, not white, were picking cotton at Tara.
sentences.zh: 她说，只有当黑人的手（而不是白人的手）在塔拉庄园采摘棉花时，她才会再次觉得自己像个贵妇。

sentences.en: So there is a race based order that she is determined to restore.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种基于种族的秩序是她决心要恢复的。

sentences.en: And the mindset that it captures is this moment when white people in America began to see themselves as the victims of racial equality,
sentences.zh: 而它所捕捉到的心态是：美国白人开始将自己视为种族平等的受害者、

sentences.en: of the victims of any movement towards civil rights.
sentences.zh: 任何民权运动的受害者的那个时刻。

sentences.en: And of course, black people do not have the power in the post-Civil War American South.
sentences.zh: 当然，黑人在内战后的美国南方并没有权力。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that I'm doing in the book is kind of fact versus fiction is really the setup of it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我在书中所做的事情之一，实际上就是将“事实与虚构”进行对比设置。

sentences.en: So I show, you know, what Mitchell claims and then go into documentary history to say what the record shows.
sentences.zh: 所以我向大家展示，你知道的，米切尔声称了什么，然后查阅文献历史去看看历史记录显示了什么。

sentences.en: And black people are very, you know, so in Scarlett's mind, black people are suddenly running the South.
sentences.zh: 黑人们——你知道的，在思嘉的心目中，黑人突然开始统治南方了。

sentences.en: Black people weren't running the South.
sentences.zh: 黑人根本没有统治南方。

sentences.zh: 所以他们所指的——他们在历史上也这样指称的——就是所谓的“黑人统治”（Negro rule）。

sentences.en: So white people under the thumb of African-Americans, what they refer to as Negro rule and saw as completely unacceptable was one black legislator or two black legislators.
sentences.zh: 因此，白人受到非裔美国人的压制，他们将这称为“黑人统治”，并认为这是完全不可接受的，而起因仅仅是一个或两个黑人议员。

sentences.en: It was having any black people in a supposedly representative multiracial democracy at all.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是在一个所谓代表性的多元种族民主国家里有任何黑人存在。

sentences.en: And they saw that as a completely unacceptable state of affairs.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种完全不可接受的现状。

sentences.en: And that is the society that they are rejecting.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们所抗拒的社会。

sentences.en: And she and her friends are determined to recreate the privileges of antebellum white slaveholding South in as many ways as they can.
sentences.zh: 她和她的朋友们决心以各种可能的方式重建内战前南方白人奴隶主的特权。

sentences.en: And that is indeed what the white South did in the aftermath of the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 这确实也是南方白人在内战结束后所做的事情。

sentences.en: And you said, you know, you wanted to catch us up on the history.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你想要让我们了解这段历史。

sentences.en: So I think we probably have to go into that is what happened then.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们可能不得不深入探讨当时究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: The white South set about recreating as many of the structures of the racial hierarchies of slavery as they could, except without slavery.
sentences.zh: 南方白人着手重建尽可能多的奴隶制种族等级结构，只不过没有了奴隶制。

sentences.en: So the problem that is faced by the slave owners, the plantocracy, once they've lost power, once they've been defeated in the Civil War, from their point of view,
sentences.zh: 因此，奴隶主、种植园主阶层在失去权力、在内战中被击败后，从他们的角度来看所面临的问题是，

sentences.en: is that people who were formerly their slaves have not only been freed, but been given the vote.
sentences.zh: 以前是他们奴隶的人不仅获得了自由，还被赋予了选举权。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And power.
sentences.zh: 以及权力。

sentences.zh: 因此，在代议制民主中拥有了权力。

sentences.en: And so if you want to kind of have to recreate a society that approximates as closely as possible to the society that existed before the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想重建一个尽可能接近内战前存在的社会的社会，

sentences.en: Well, that starts so quickly, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这开始得太快了。

sentences.en: And then what you do, you create pretexts to lock black people up so that you can make them felons.

sentences.zh: 所以帕奇曼（Parchman）就是密西西比州立监狱，因为它以前就是帕奇曼种植园。

sentences.en: And Angola in Louisiana, which is the federal penitentiary there, which is notorious because it's a death row prison, it's known locally just as the farm.
sentences.zh: 而路易斯安那州的安哥拉（Angola），那里的联邦监狱因关押死刑犯而臭名昭著，当地人就直接称它为“农场”。

sentences.en: You've been sent down to the farm, right?
sentences.zh: 你被送到底下的农场去了，对吧？

sentences.en: So they, and they, because it's built on an old plantation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们——而且由于它是建在旧种植园上的。

sentences.zh: 让我问你关于种植园的事，因为很显然，《乱世佳人》不仅是一部关于一个女人的电影，它是一部关于一个地方的电影。

sentences.en: For other purposes, doing a different podcast a couple of years ago, I downloaded their wedding brochure and was,

sentences.zh: 在想，在这个曾经有成千上万的人作为奴隶生、作为奴隶死的种植园遗址上结婚会是怎样一种体验。

sentences.en: So what's your take on the sort of, do you think Gone with, I mean, Gone with the Wind clearly enshrines the plantation as this place of kind of vanished beauty, this civilization,
sentences.zh: 所以你对这种……你觉得《乱世佳人》——我的意思是，《乱世佳人》显然将种植园奉为一种消逝的美丽、一种文明的圣地，

sentences.en: you know, lost in the wind of time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在时间的风中迷失了。

sentences.en: Do you think that has, that era has died and that now most Americans have a very different view of plantations?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那个时代已经消亡，现在的绝大多数美国人对种植园有着截然不同的看法吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think that myth is too deeply entrenched ever to be sort of dislodged?
sentences.zh: 还是你觉得这种神话已经根深蒂固，永远无法被动摇？

sentences.en: Well, I think it can be dislodged, but I don't think it has been yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它是可以被动摇的，但我认为它还没有被动摇。

sentences.en: And I think that what we see is this kind of extraordinary cognitive dissonance where people can hold these two completely contradictory ideas in their head at the same time and not think about them.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们看到的是一种非同寻常的认知失调，人们可以在脑海中同时持有这两种完全矛盾的观点，却对它们视而不见。

sentences.en: And so they can say very easily, yes, slavery was wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以非常轻松地说，是的，奴隶制是错的。

sentences.en: Slavery was bad and put themselves in hoop skirts and go get married at Boone Hall and imagine that that was all lovely.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as you say, but for a certain type of imagination, we would be thinking about the historical realities of that place.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，但对于某种特定类型的想象力来说，我们本该去思考那个地方的历史现实。

sentences.en: And to me, and I say this, and I know people don't always take kindly to these comparisons.
sentences.zh: 对我和我所说的话而言——我知道人们并不总是乐于接受这种比较。

sentences.en: I think they completely hold up in this case.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这种情况下，这种比较完全站得住脚。

sentences.en: To me, it's like getting married at Dachau.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这就像是在达豪集中营举办婚礼一样。

sentences.en: I mean, it is literally like romanticizing a concentration camp.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直就像是在将集中营浪漫化。

sentences.en: But the mythology allows for there to be these two separate versions where people talk about slavery as if it happened in a way that was distinct from this.
sentences.zh: 但这种神话允许存在这两种截然不同的版本，人们谈论奴隶制时，就好像它发生的方式与这种现实毫无关系一样。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I tried to think about a lot in writing this is kind of how does that work and how does that happen?
sentences.zh: 我在写作时反复思考的一个问题是，这究竟是如何运作的，又是如何发生的？

sentences.en: And it seems to me that one of the things that happens is that we use these cliched ideas, cliched language or cliched images that stop us from thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，其中发生的一点是，我们使用了这些陈腐的观点、陈腐的语言或陈腐的意象，从而阻碍了我们去真正思考它。

sentences.en: So you can talk about an ideal slave plantation.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以谈论一个理想的奴隶种植园。

sentences.zh: 这是一个人们经常使用的短语，一个理想的奴隶种植园。

sentences.en: And again, to estrange people from that, I put concentration camp there and go, what would happen if you talked about an ideal concentration camp?
sentences.zh: 同样，为了让人们对这种说法感到陌生和警醒，我把“集中营”放进去，然后问：如果你谈论一个“理想的集中营”，会发生什么？

sentences.en: It's insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It's morally deranged.
sentences.zh: 这是道义上的错乱。

sentences.en: And yet people will still talk about an ideal slave plantation and be like, well, it was bad for African-Americans.
sentences.zh: 然而人们仍然会谈论一个理想的奴隶种植园，并觉得，嗯，这对非裔美国人来说确实不好。

sentences.en: Yeah, I grant that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我承认这点。

sentences.en: OK, maybe, you know, and it's like, no, you've got a complete this is this this mythology was there to insist that it really wasn't that bad after all.
sentences.zh: 行吧，也许，你知道的，这就好比，不，你完全陷入了——这个神话的存在就是为了坚称它其实并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: So once you've gone down that road, what do you then do with Gone with the Wind?
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你沿着这条路走下去，你接下来该怎么对待《乱世佳人》？

sentences.en: Because, you know, here you've got a film that embeds that idea that turns Scarlett O'Hara into a victim and her family are their victiMs.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，在这里你有一部电影，它巩固了那种理念，将思嘉·奥哈拉（Scarlett O'Hara）塑造成受害者，而她的家人也是受害者。

sentences.en: It's hard to watch Gone with the Wind now, I would say, without wincing.
sentences.zh: 我想说，现在看《乱世佳人》很难不感到尴尬抽搐。

sentences.en: I mean, you can be the most unwoke person imaginable and you will still watch that film and find bits that will make you wince and cringe and just think, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以成为你能想象到的最缺乏政治觉悟（unwoke）的人，但你依然会在看那部电影时发现某些片段让你感到畏缩、尴尬，只会感叹：哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And it's a lot less racist than the novel.
sentences.zh: 而且它比原著小说受到的种族主义影响要少得多。

sentences.zh: 我能引用一下马丁·达灵顿（Martin Darlington）的话吗？

sentences.zh: “我实在喜欢不起来这种对逝去时代的极其露骨的怀旧情绪。”

sentences.en: Why is it still a regular in best film ever made lists?
sentences.zh: 为什么它至今仍是“有史以来最佳电影”榜单上的常客？

sentences.en: It's confederate propaganda.
sentences.zh: 这就是南部邦联的宣传片。

So, so, so implicit in that, you know, it is still.

sentences.zh: 它是经典好莱坞电影的伟大胜利。

sentences.en: I mean, because Sarah said it's, it, it's part of, of, well, it's kind of bred of that yearning of fantasy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如莎拉所说，它——它——它是由那种对幻想的渴望所孕育出来的，不是吗？

sentences.en: That the, the, the Great Depression, you know, so the Wizard of Oz and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 大萧条时期的产物，你知道的，比如《绿野仙踪》和所有这类东西。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not as great a film as, as an arguably an even more racist film, Birth of a Nation, which is a colossal technical achievement.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它并不是一部像可以说是更加种族主义的电影《一个国家的诞生》那样伟大的电影，后者可是一项极其宏大的技术成就。

sentences.en: Yes, so, so these are, these are totemic films in the, in the history of Hollywood and therefore of world cinema.
sentences.zh: 对，所以，这些是，这些是好莱坞乃至世界电影史上的标志性电影。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of, what do you do with them?
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，你该拿它们怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's the question, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在，对吧？

sentences.en: So, and some people will say what we have to do is stop watching them and stop reading them and stop talking about them.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人会说，我们必须做的是停止观看它们，停止阅读它们，停止谈论它们。

sentences.en: And there are people who've made that case very forcefully and would disagree with my bringing it back into the conversation and saying, this is something that, that,
sentences.zh: 有些人非常有力地提出了这种观点，并不同意我把它重新带回对话中，并说，这是某些，某些，

sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要去思考的事情。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这是一个持续存在的问题，我们该如何处理我们自己历史中这些有问题的叙事，我们该拿它们怎么办？

sentences.en: My view is I'd rather confront them, dismantle them and think about what they're there for.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，我宁愿直面它们，解构它们，并思考它们存在的意义。

sentences.en: And, and, and because if we just try to put them to one side, then what we've discovered is that people still just take what they want from them.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，因为如果我们只是试图把它们放到一边，那么我们就会发现，人们仍然会从中各取所需。

sentences.en: Unless you actually think that we should censor them, which I don't believe.
sentences.zh: 除非你真的认为我们应该审查它们，但我并不这么认为。

sentences.en: And I don't think anybody, you know, in this conversation believes.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在这个对话中的任何人，你知道，都不这么认为。

sentences.en: So because I, I,
sentences.zh: 所以因为我，我，

sentences.en: one of the examples that I use fairly early on in the book is that there were some people present at the insurrection in 2021 saying that Gone with the Wind was their favorite book,
sentences.zh: 我在书的早期使用的一个例子是，在2021年的国会山骚乱中，有一些人在现场说《乱世佳人》是他们最喜欢的书，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So you've got people who are still going to read this story and encounter it.
sentences.zh: 所以你会发现，仍然有人会去阅读这个故事并接触到它。

sentences.en: And if you do it without any kind of pushback, again, unless you're going to try to destroy it, which good luck with that, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你没有任何形式的抵制，再说一次，除非你打算试图摧毁它——祝你好运，对吧？

sentences.en: That's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: Um, so given that it's out there and that people are encountering it, I think that the best thing that we can do is try to problematize it as much as we can and to,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以既然它已经存在，而且人们正在接触它，我认为我们能做的最好的事情就是尽我们所能去将其问题化，并且，

sentences.en: and to make sure that, um, that people are educated about, about what it means and what it's saying.
sentences.zh: 并且确保，嗯，人们能够接受教育，了解它意味着什么以及它在表达什么。

sentences.en: But also for me, it's to recognize that it captures all kinds of important truths about how we got where we are.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这也是为了认识到，它捕捉到了关于我们如何走到今天的各种重要真相。

sentences.en: And if, and if we deny it in the, in the sense of saying, well, you know, I want to, I want to, I don't want to,
sentences.zh: 而且如果，如果我们去否认它，那种觉得“好吧，你知道，我想，我想，我不想……”的心态，

sentences.en: it's actually a very scarlet thing to do is I'll think about that tomorrow.

sentences.en: I don't want to think about that right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在不想考虑这个。

sentences.en: Um, it's, it's, it's a troublesome thought.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个令人烦恼的想法。

sentences.en: Um, well, it is a troublesome thought, but the problem is, is that it captures, it captures a historical reality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是一个令人烦恼的想法，但问题在于，它捕捉到了，它捕捉到了历史的现实。

sentences.en: Um, the myth is itself a historical reality, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，神话本身就是一种历史现实，对吧？

sentences.en: The mythology happened and it, and it changed political reality in all kinds of ways in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这种神话确实发生了，并且它在全美以各种方式改变了政治现实。

sentences.en: And that has consequences now, regardless of whether we know about it or understand it.
sentences.zh: 无论我们是否了解或理解它，这在现在都会产生后果。

sentences.en: And so for me, understanding this mythology helps things like the storming of the Capitol in 2021 makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，理解这种神话有助于理解2021年国会山骚乱这样的事情。

sentences.en: And that's kind of one of the key arguments I make in the book is that, is that if you understand this stuff,
sentences.zh: 这也是我在书中提出的核心论点之一，那就是，如果你理解了这些东西，

sentences.en: then at least you can understand where we are and it starts to become intelligible.
sentences.zh: 那么至少你能理解我们身处何地，事情也开始变得可以理解了。

sentences.en: And so I do it on the basis of know your enemy, you know, I mean, we have to know what it is that we're combating in order to combat it.
sentences.zh: 所以我这样做是基于“了解你的敌人”的原则，我的意思是，为了与之搏斗，我们必须了解我们在与什么搏斗。

sentences.en: It seems to me, and this is a kind of, although Gone with the Wind is a reason is an incredibly long book.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，尽管《乱世佳人》是一本极其厚重的书。

sentences.en: It's still a reasonably, um, discreet and self-contained entity for understanding a very, very complex history.
sentences.zh: 对于理解一段非常非常复杂的历史来说，它仍然是一个相当独立且自足的实体。

sentences.en: So Sarah, would you say, I'm obviously the birth of a nation would be another contender.
sentences.zh: 那么萨拉，你会说——显然《一个国家的诞生》将是另一个竞争者。

sentences.en: Would you say this is a film, has there been a film that in your view that has had such a bail?
sentences.zh: 你会说这是一部电影吗？在你看来，有没有哪部电影曾产生过如此巨大的——

sentences.en: I mean, you clearly think it's had a really baleful effect on American culture, politics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你显然认为它对美国文化和政治产生了非常恶劣的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, is it the worst in your view because it was so successful and because it's so deeply enshrined the idea of the lost cause?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在你看来它是最糟糕的吗？因为它如此成功，并且因为它如此根深蒂固地树立了“南方邦联之失”的理念？

sentences.en: I should say, I was at two things in answer to that.
sentences.zh: 我得说，为了回答这个问题，我要提两点。

sentences.en: One is that, cause I haven't said this yet and it's important.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，因为我还没说过这个，而且这很重要。

sentences.en: And since Tom said, you know, you barely saw it and barely remember it.
sentences.zh: 既然汤姆说过，你知道，你几乎没看过它，也几乎不记得它了。

sentences.en: I need to say for listeners that, you know, I grew up watching this movie and reading this book and I loved the movie.
sentences.zh: 我需要对听众说的是，你知道，我是看着这部电影、读着这本书长大的，我非常喜欢这部电影。

sentences.en: I mean, I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我爱死它了。

sentences.en: So I'm very much an apostate here and it's important to understand that because I also understand the feelings of those who love it.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这里很大程度上算是一个叛道者，理解这一点很重要，因为我也能理解那些喜欢它的人的感受。

sentences.en: But I have come to believe that it had a baleful influence on my society.
sentences.zh: 但我已经开始相信，它对我的社会产生了恶劣的影响。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: The baleful influence is because you love it.
sentences.zh: 之所以有恶劣的影响，正是因为你喜欢它。

sentences.en: I mean, it's because it's effective.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是因为它很有效力。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's effective and powerful and Scott Harrell is an amazing character and it's great.
sentences.zh: 对，它既有效力又极具力量，而且斯嘉丽·奥哈拉（Scott Harrell）是个了不起的角色，它棒极了。

sentences.en: And so, but then it, yeah, and it convinces you to think all kinds of things that on second thought, I don't think I want to think.
sentences.zh: 所以，但随后它，对，它说服你去相信各种各样的事情，而在三思之后，我觉得我并不想去相信它们。

sentences.en: And that's the process of what I'm trying to take people through with the book.
sentences.zh: 这就是我试图通过这本书带读者经历的过程。

sentences.en: But to answer Dom's question directly, no, I think Birth of a Nation was probably worse.
sentences.zh: 但要直接回答多姆（Dom）的问题，不，我认为《一个国家的诞生》可能更糟糕。

sentences.en: And the reason I say that is because it directly inspired the rebirth of the Klan in 1915.
sentences.zh: 我这么说的原因是因为它直接启发了1915年三K党的死灰复燃。

sentences.en: And we know that we can, there's all kinds of ways in which that's documented.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，可以通过各种方式证明这一点，这是有据可查的。

sentences.en: And so it led directly to the torture and murder of thousands of African Americans in the early decades of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 因此，它直接导致了20世纪头几十年成千上万非裔美国人的遭受酷刑与谋杀。

sentences.en: It's not clear to me that the Gone with the Wind has documented the same direct murderous outcome that Birth of a Nation had.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，《乱世佳人》并没有像《一个国家的诞生》那样被记录下直接导致谋杀的后果。

sentences.en: But, and, you know, Birth of a Nation affected politics in a more, and I am going to use this word,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，《一个国家的诞生》对政治的影响更具，我打算用这个词，

sentences.en: unreconstructed kind of a way where Gone with the Wind was challenged from the moment that it came out, partly because of Birth of a Nation.
sentences.zh: 一种未经改造的、原教旨般的方式，而《乱世佳人》从它问世的那一刻起就受到了挑战，部分原因正是因为《一个国家的诞生》。

sentences.en: So African Americans were pushing back against Gone with the Wind from the second that it emerged.
sentences.zh: 所以非裔美国人从它出现的那一秒起就在抵制《乱世佳人》。

sentences.en: So it was,
sentences.zh: 所以它，

sentences.en: it never had such an unproblematic effect on the culture as Birth of a Nation was allowed to have for several decades would have enjoyed this kind of sway over white culture.
sentences.zh: 它对文化从未产生过像《一个国家的诞生》在几十年里被允许的那种毫无争议的影响，那种对白人文化的影响。

sentences.en: So I think that was even worse, but that's a race to the bottom, as we might say.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那个更糟，但正如我们所说，这是五十步笑百步。

sentences.en: And I'd certainly not to excuse Gone with the Wind.
sentences.zh: 而且我当然不是在为《乱世佳人》开脱。

sentences.en: Well, Sarah, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，萨拉，非常感谢。

sentences.en: That was a brilliant exposition.
sentences.zh: 这是一次精彩的讲解。

sentences.en: And I hope you have all enjoyed what's five episodes now we've done on the American Civil War, incredibly complex and important.
sentences.zh: 我希望大家都喜欢我们已经完成的关于美国内战的五集节目，这 incredibly 复杂且重要。

sentences.en: The question is whether this podcast will send people rushing to watch Gone with the Wind and what Sarah would think about that.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这个播客会不会引发人们蜂拥去观看《乱世佳人》，而萨拉对此会怎么想。

sentences.en: I guess you wouldn't be unhappy, would you, if people were watching Gone with the Wind on the back of this podcast?
sentences.zh: 我想如果人们因为这个播客而去观看《乱世佳人》，你不会不高兴吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I'll be honest with you and say I'd rather they were reading my book.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老实说，我更希望他们读我的书。

sentences.en: I mean, all facetiousness aside, if they are, I would hope that they would read my book too and to understand the way that they're in dialogue.
sentences.zh: 抛开所有俏皮话不谈，如果他们真的去看了，我希望他们也能读读我的书，去理解它们之间是如何对话的。

sentences.en: Okay, so Sarah's book, The Wrath to Come, Gone with the Wind and The Lies America Tells.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是萨拉的书，《将临之怒：《乱世佳人》与美国谎言》（The Wrath to Come, Gone with the Wind and The Lies America Tells）。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，萨拉。

sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.zh: 我们很快再见。
